# E-OPEN-SOURCE-001 — Open-source the engine as Master Console (AGPL-3.0): anchor, clean, rewrite, rebrand, announce

- **Epic label and number:** E-OPEN-SOURCE-001
- **Title:** Open-source the engine as Master Console (AGPL-3.0): anchor, clean, rewrite, rebrand, announce
- **Owner:** Alex α (orchestration) with ε for sprint execution; operator approves the irreversible gates
- **Parent roadmap area:** distribution / public launch
- **Goal:** Make the public repo cygaco/MC safe, honest and accurately described as Master Console (AGPL-3.0), with the prior-art evidence (April 2026 commits + tag warpos@0.1.4) provably untouched, so the operator can announce: "I kept building things months before the labs announced them; here are the receipts."

(4 marks) → drop 'Master Control'. The security lane returned FAIL on `open-source/S-OS-06` @ `f666c702` (GPT-5.5 via codex, record `d-mu0b4omb-9e2a28c7`, ~21:15Z, full text `runtime/S-OS-06/gauntlet/security-gpt-result.out`), so the branch cannot land and β r4 (gauntlet→release) must not be consulted until the lane is GREEN. Four findings, each re-verified against the code during the 2026-09-13 tracker reconcile rather than taken from the report: (1) HIGH — the disposition model is LINE-scoped rather than occurrence-scoped at `scripts/open-source/partition-loader.js:511` and `scripts/open-source/rename-mc.js:625`, so one registered compat occurrence or pin on a line launders every other live slug on that same line and games the per-category delta assertion β r3c required; (2) HIGH — the F8 freeze-history check at `scripts/open-source/partition-loader.js:926` runs `git log --no-merges`, so a compat or allow-list widening introduced directly in a MERGE commit evades the separate-amendment-commit rule (confirmed: the `--no-merges` flag is on that line); (3) HIGH — the raw-env guard at `tests/regression/S-OS-06/raw-env-scan.js:18` is not case-insensitive (`PREFIX_ALT` is built uppercase-only and the three patterns at lines 21–23 carry no `i` flag, confirmed by reading the file), and because `process.env` is case-insensitive on Windows, lowercase dot reads, bracket reads and destructuring all bypass the helper — note the backend re-review's PASS 98 covered the case-insensitivity fix at a DIFFERENT site (`8effe80d`), so both sites need checking; (4) MEDIUM — `scripts/checks/record-trust-exit.js` and the whole `tests/regression/S-OS-06/*.test.js` suite are unreachable from `npm test` (the script is `node --test "scripts/**/*.test.js"`, confirmed by reading `package.json`) and from `leak-gate`, so the CI green that serves as the landing precondition never exercised the exit gate or the sprint's falsifier suite. Required fix: fix-cycle r2 (attempt 2 of 3 under the frozen 3-attempt halt criterion), then a security re-review. The test-glob half of finding 4 is a `package.json` edit and is allowed; if the workflow file itself must change, the classifier denies it and the exact edit goes to the operator.
